passage.text: A few years ago, Mr. Brown received an invitation to the wedding of his old friend Steve.
passage.reading: ə ˈfjuː ˈjɪrz əˈɡoʊ, ˈmɪstər ˈbraʊn rɪˈsiːvd ən ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃən tə ðə ˈwɛdɪŋ əv hɪz ˈoʊld ˈfrɛnd ˈstiːv.

passage.text: The wedding was at a big hotel in Bangkok on a Saturday afternoon.
passage.reading: ðə ˈwɛdɪŋ wʌz ət ə ˈbɪɡ hoʊˈtɛl ɪn ˈbæŋkɑːk ɑːn ə ˈsætərdeɪ ˌæftərˈnuːn.

passage.text: Mr. Brown arrived late and hurried into the hall just as the wedding was starting.
passage.reading: ˈmɪstər ˈbraʊn əˈraɪvd ˈleɪt ənd ˈhɜːrid ˈɪntuː ðə ˈhɔːl dʒʌst əz ðə ˈwɛdɪŋ wʌz ˈstɑːrtɪŋ.

passage.text: The hall was full, so he sat at the back.
passage.reading: ðə ˈhɔːl wʌz ˈfʊl, soʊ hiː ˈsæt ət ðə ˈbæk.

passage.text: He didn't know anyone, but he wasn't surprised, because Steve had a lot of friends.
passage.reading: hiː ˈdɪdənt ˈnoʊ ˈɛniwʌn, bʌt hiː ˈwʌzənt sərˈpraɪzd, bɪˈkɔːz ˈstiːv ˈhæd ə ˈlɑːt əv ˈfrɛndz.

passage.text: Then the bride walked in with her new husband, and everyone stood up.
passage.reading: ˈðɛn ðə ˈbraɪd ˈwɔːkt ˈɪn wɪð hɜːr ˈnuː ˈhʌzbənd, ənd ˈɛvriwʌn ˈstʊd ˈʌp.

passage.text: Mr. Brown looked at the husband, and his mouth fell open.
passage.reading: ˈmɪstər ˈbraʊn ˈlʊkt ət ðə ˈhʌzbənd, ənd hɪz ˈmaʊθ ˈfɛl ˈoʊpən.

passage.text: To his horror, he realized that he was at the wrong wedding.
passage.reading: tə hɪz ˈhɔːrər, hiː ˈriːəlaɪzd ðæt hiː wʌz ət ðə ˈrɔːŋ ˈwɛdɪŋ.

passage.text: Just then, the host asked if any guests would like to give a speech.
passage.reading: dʒʌst ˈðɛn, ðə ˈhoʊst ˈæskt ɪf ˈɛni ˈɡɛsts wʊd ˈlaɪk tə ˈɡɪv ə ˈspiːtʃ.

passage.text: The man next to Mr. Brown said, "You're the only foreigner here. You should say something!"
passage.reading: ðə ˈmæn ˈnɛkst tə ˈmɪstər ˈbraʊn ˈsɛd, jʊr ði ˈoʊnli ˈfɔːrənər ˈhɪr. juː ʃʊd ˈseɪ ˈsʌmθɪŋ!

passage.text: Mr. Brown went red, but everyone was looking at him.
passage.reading: ˈmɪstər ˈbraʊn ˈwɛnt ˈrɛd, bʌt ˈɛvriwʌn wʌz ˈlʊkɪŋ ət hɪm.

passage.text: So he stood up and said, "Congratulations! I wish you a long and happy life together."
passage.reading: soʊ hiː ˈstʊd ˈʌp ənd ˈsɛd, kənˌɡrætʃəˈleɪʃənz! aɪ ˈwɪʃ juː ə ˈlɔːŋ ənd ˈhæpi ˈlaɪf təˈɡɛðər.

passage.text: Everyone smiled, and he quickly sneaked out of the hall.
passage.reading: ˈɛvriwʌn ˈsmaɪld, ənd hiː ˈkwɪkli ˈsniːkt ˈaʊt əv ðə ˈhɔːl.

passage.text: Steve's wedding was in the next hall, and it had already started.
passage.reading: ˈstiːvz ˈwɛdɪŋ wʌz ɪn ðə ˈnɛkst ˈhɔːl, ənd ɪt hæd ɔːlˈrɛdi ˈstɑːrtɪd.

passage.text: When Steve heard the story, he laughed so much that he told it in his own wedding speech.
passage.reading: wɛn ˈstiːv ˈhɜːrd ðə ˈstɔːri, hiː ˈlæft soʊ ˈmʌtʃ ðæt hiː ˈtoʊld ɪt ɪn hɪz ˈoʊn ˈwɛdɪŋ ˈspiːtʃ.

passage.text: Now Mr. Brown always reads an invitation twice!
passage.reading: ˈnaʊ ˈmɪstər ˈbraʊn ˈɔːlweɪz ˈriːdz ən ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃən ˈtwaɪs!
